title: Tennessee Eastman reactor pressure states under Fault 2
research_question: Does a reactor-pressure rate construction selected on one Fault 2 simulation run, and frozen, produce the same rising, falling and inactive partition on the other Fault 2 runs, and does it stay quiet on normal-operation windows?
data_source: Tennessee Eastman Process simulation data, Fault 2, simulation runs 1 to 10, as distributed in the Rieth et al. 2017 dataset; the reactor_pressure and time_(h) columns of each run, 3,001 rows per run.

observation_schema.unit: hours since the start of the run
derived first difference of the envelope

time_semantics: Each row is a sample at an instant; the simulator writes one row every three minutes.
preprocessing_steps: reactor_pressure_smooth is the rolling maximum of reactor_pressure over rolling_max_window rows, then the rolling mean over rolling_mean_window rows, shifted by offline_alignment_shift rows
reactor_pressure_change is the first difference of reactor_pressure_smooth
time_step_hours is the first difference of time_(h)
reactor_pressure_rate is reactor_pressure_change divided by time_step_hours
rows where any derived column is undefined are excluded and counted
object_definition: One row of the result is one rising occurrence of the smoothed reactor pressure: the interval from the first rising sample to the last, with the exit event on the last rising sample.
measurements: count of rising occurrences per run
start and end time of each rising occurrence in hours
duration of each rising occurrence in hours
pressure gained within each occurrence in kPa
validations: states are mutually exclusive and cover every valid observation
every run compiles to 3,001 observations with 99 excluded, 49 leading and 50 trailing
the partition on runs 1 to 9 matches the published construction row for row
claim_limits: the construction is a repeatable abnormal-pressure representation, not a Fault 2 classifier
no claim is made about faults other than Fault 2
